title: C3 data-socket frame
description: Every chunk on a session's data socket (conn-{conn_id}/{socket}, both directions) is a 24-byte envelope followed by its payload (lang-arch §4.1 amendment 2026-09-14; decision 5.14). The payload is unframed terminal data: strip every envelope and what remains is the byte stream lang-arch §4.1 describes. The binary layout below is normative and the fixtures' .bin files are its ground truth; this schema describes the decoded form the fixtures use. seq on an output frame is immortality §4.1's per-session monotonic sequence number (LOCKED): worker-assigned, from 1, the number the core's last_committed_seq will refer to. seq on an input frame is the core's own per-session counter, from 1 — explicitly not the §4.1 number; the corpus numbers only output, and decision 5.24's rule (per session) applies to both. Each is strictly increasing; a jump (frames dropped while no core was attached) is allowed, a repeat or a decrease is not. timestamp is nanoseconds since the Unix epoch: for output, the worker's clock when it read the bytes from the target, always (immortality §4.2, LOCKED); for input, the core's clock when it sends the frame. The two directions are stamped by two clocks, so a reader never assumes timestamps increase across directions. Trust is SO_PEERCRED, as on every C3 socket: a data socket accepts a peer only when its uid is the TSB service uid (immortality §6.1, LOCKED). The gap frame (decision 5.14: the gap marker is a flagged empty frame, not an out-of-band message; immortality §4.3): a worker loses output the core has not received only while no core peer holds the session's data socket — with a peer attached a slow core is backpressure, and from hello to live the worker does not read that channel (ipc-control.schema.json) — so every loss is known when hello_ack is sent, and a gap frame appears only in a handshake's replay, before its first replayed frame. It is an output frame with flags bit 1 set and no payload: seq is first_buffered_seq - 1, the last lost seq, so it never shares a number with a frame the ring still holds; timestamp is hello_ack's last_dropped_ts. length is 0 exactly when bit 1 is set, and bit 1 is never set on an input frame. Only PTY sessions have a ring, so only they ever carry one. The data frame's version stays 1: the gap bit is additive, and only a v0.2 core, which asked for the replay, ever receives a gap frame. Sizes: an output frame's payload is at most the connection's buffer_bytes, an input frame's at most its input_frame_max (both on connect); a worker refuses a longer input frame from its header alone (input_refused too_large). A recording hold closes this session's data peer, suppresses redial until restart and refuses input recording_unavailable (terminal-output-accounting §5.3; owed). The ordinary data path (Tu, 2026-09-27): a session's data socket that ends alone is not an end. The core waits a moment for a control-side end; when none comes it re-dials the socket — once for each such loss — through the same trusted dial, the worker takes the newer core peer, and the handshake replays what the dead socket lost. A re-dial that fails, the socket refusing or missing, is E10 once the core has re-read the spool for the session and found no end there: terminated / worker_lost (session model §9, §13), so no session is left with no data path and no end. When the connection's control socket still answers, the core then sends close_channel for that session, so the worker does not keep a channel no core records. Outside a recording hold, from the loss until its handshake reaches live the core forwards no client input and answers it on C2 with input_refused replaying. When a session ends, the worker writes its last output frame and then closes that data peer: that EOF after the end, not the end event alone, tells the core its recording holds the session's output (ipc-control.schema.json release). The core tells attached clients about an interrupted data path with the C2 data_path frame.

flags.description: Bit 0 is the direction, bit 1 the gap marker (output only, so 3 never occurs). Every other bit is 0 at this tag.

direction.description: Bit 0 of flags, spelled out: out = target → core (0), in = core → target (1).

length.description: Payload bytes: at least 1 on a data frame, 0 exactly on a gap frame.

oneOf.description: A data frame: output or input, with a payload.
The gap frame: output, bit 1 set, no payload.

fields.name: version
fields.note: 1 at this tag. A receiver refuses a version it does not speak.

fields.name: flags
fields.note: bit 0 direction: 0 = target → core (output), 1 = core → target (input). bit 1 gap: the frame declares that output before it was lost; set only on output, and only with length 0. bits 2-7 are 0.

fields.name: length
fields.note: Payload bytes that follow the header; 0 exactly on a gap frame.

fields.name: seq
fields.note: Per session, per direction, from 1. A gap frame's is the last lost seq.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.note: Nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC. A gap frame's is the stamp of the last frame the ring dropped.

x-binary-layout.payload: `length` bytes of terminal data, unframed, immediately after the header; none on a gap frame.
